title: I SEE THE DEMON — Creepy Elements, but Lacks A Lasting Punch
content:
Review by Steve Barton II

Science fiction and horror are genres that can mix together perfectly, but sometimes the balance is completely off. It’s a delicate balancing act between the two styles and substance has only been achieved by masters like Ridley Scott with Alien and Steven Spielberg with Close Encounters of the Third Kind. In Jacob Lees Johnson’s new film I See the Demon, there are some large ideas that didn’t quite fit into this small independent film. I See the Demon follows Lucy (Alexis Zollicoffer) as she arrives home to learn that there is a surprise birthday party happening for her, but she’s not in the best state for a celebration with friends. As Lucy starts seeing unexplainable horrific visions and becoming disoriented by her surroundings, she wonders if she will ever escape from this nightmare of a reality.

Immediately, this movie starts off in a very strange and unsettling way with odd sounds with an extremely dark frame. It sets the mood perfectly, because the movie is confusing and hard to explain, but still entertaining nonetheless. The weird imagery and flashes of spooky creatures is effective, but there are long stretches that lose all the tension built up. Other sci-fi/horror movies have their in-between moments where they build up the characters and plot, but I See the Demon doesn’t have the same level of cast members nor a variety of settings to keep those scenes interesting.

The cast of I See the Demon is full of mostly unknown actors in their first starring roles, but one familiar face is almost more distracting rather than serving as a fun cameo. Millennials and fans of cult comedies will recognize Jon Heder from his career defining role as Napoleon Dynamite and he’s been riding that wave since 2004. In I See the Demon, Jon plays Roger who is Lucy’s friend and serves mostly as the comedic relief of the group who takes the piss out of everyone’s conversations. He’s often more annoying than he is funny, but the characters react negatively too so it may have been intentional, but it’s hard to gauge. Dave Martinez as Billy embodies the Ash from Alien role in a lot of ways with his responses and demeanor and it helps make the atmosphere feel even more unnatural.

I See the Demon has some interesting elements, but it doesn’t land on being a groundbreaking science fiction horror movie. The lighting and cinematography during the haunting moments looks great, but the lack of any other setting outside of this house gets stale and not the intended claustrophobic feel. The cast of characters aren’t bad, but they come across very thin and lack genuine personalities that have any unique characteristics. Napoleon tried to break through the boring moments with obnoxious humor, but it delivers more bothersome rather than funny. Films like I See the Demon have their audiences who enjoy the mystery and connecting the breadcrumbs, but it won’t work for the masses. It’s up to you now, will you be like Lucy and say “I See the Demon”? 

I See the Demon is available on VOD platforms stating October 20th!

Rating: 2.5/5
